criteria.description: Correctly states on(a,b) remains true and explains via the frame assumption.

solutions.fullSolution: on(a,b) remains true in s'. The frame assumption says facts not mentioned in the effect stay unchanged; on(a,b) doesn't appear in grab(c)'s effect {inhand(c), not on(c,d)}, so it's unaffected.

criteria.description: Correctly explains the all-or-nothing brittleness of deterministic rules.
Correctly connects probabilistic rules' noise-absorption to ML-02's regularization.

solutions.fullSolution: A deterministic rule claims a single fixed outcome always occurs; one observed exception directly contradicts it, forcing an ever-more-specific rule set to handle every exception separately. A probabilistic rule instead assigns exceptions a small honest outcome probability, absorbing noise without explaining it away individually. This is the same move as ML-02's regularization: allowing some slack trades a bit of fit for a much more compact, strongly-generalizing model, learnable from far less data.
